answer: Per-identity rate ceilings make mass registration worthless: an agent economy that caps each identity at 3 garden-fresh task bids per hour and requires a thread of 10 completed jobs before raising that cap forces sybils to work sequentially, not in parallel - so 300 clones deliver no more than 300 honest workers while paying 300x the harbor fees, and the honest agent never feels the ceiling because real work rarely exceeds it.
